less_stable.text: When opponents play a defensive return to Lee's mid backhand, Lee loses the point within two shots 23% of the time (n=35, 95% CI 12%-39%); typical pros lose 9% after the same shot (difference +14 points, 95% CI +3 to +30, n=1899).

When Lee pushes or rushes to the opponent's rear backhand, Lee loses the point within two shots 19% of the time (n=36, 95% CI 10%-35%); typical pros lose 8% after the same shot (difference +11 points, 95% CI +1 to +27, n=1430).

When opponents play a net shot to Lee's front backhand, Lee loses the point within two shots 8% of the time (n=136, 95% CI 5%-14%); typical pros lose 14% after the same shot (difference -6 points, 95% CI -10 to 0, n=6722).

coach.against_reference: Attack the two situations listed under 'What Lee should fix': that is where Lee loses more often than typical pros.

xp.caveat: Read this first: xP from shot and position data has no signal mid-rally in elite singles (holdout AUC 0.50 on strokes that did not end the rally). The same features reach AUC 0.79 only on final strokes, where the task is classifying how an already-decisive stroke ends (winner or error), not predicting a rally. Nothing in this section is a working expected-points model.
